detail: ROS Peacekeeping example (peace.R): survival / censored time-to-ceasefire-failure, one row per conflict episode (country-conflict); delay is the time, censored? the indicator. No repeated cluster.

ROS PearsonLee example: frequency-weighted table of child vs parent heights (regress child ~ parent). frequency is a weight; gp/par/chl are parent-child sex labels (4 combinations), no sampling cluster.
ROS Pollution example: 60 SMSA cities, one row per city (McDonald-Schwing mortality regression) mort ~ pollution + demographics; no grouping factor.
Stata twin of Pollution/data/pollution.csv; 60 cities, one row per city, no grouping factor.
ROS Poststrat example: 778 respondents (vote and pid = party, 3 levels, the predictor); one row per respondent, no sampling cluster.
ROS RiskyBehavior example (risky.R): Poisson/neg-bin glm of fupacts (follow-up unprotected acts) on treatment (couples/women_alone); one row per subject, no repeated cluster.
ROS Roaches example (roaches.R): Poisson glm of y (roach count) ~ roach1 + treatment + senior with offset exposure2; one row per apartment, no grouping factor.
ROS SIS data: 1501 persons, income/benefit components; one row per person, no grouping factor.
Raw Stata source (28 cols) of Sesame/data/sesame.csv (filed in the registry); same 240 children, duplicate of the Sesame study.
ROS Student (UCI math course): one row per student; school is a 2-level fixed predictor (GP/MS) used among 26 covariates in stan_glm(G3mat ~ .), not a sampling cluster.
ROS Student merged-all (682 rows): one row per student, school a 2-level fixed predictor, no grouping factor.
ROS Student merged math+Portuguese (students common to both): one row per student, 2-level school predictor, no grouping factor.
ROS Student (UCI Portuguese course): one row per student, school a 2-level fixed predictor, no sampling cluster; stan_glm(G3por ~ .) classical.
ROS Names example: wide table, 98012 names x 134 year-count columns (X1880..X2010); a name-by-year count matrix, no grouping factor (wide format).

ROS Beauty example (beauty.R): classical stan_glm(eval ~ beauty + female), one row per course evaluation. course_id is unusable as a cluster: 306 of 463 rows carry the catch-all 0, lumping many single-taught courses into one pseudo-group.
ROS Bypass example: 200 patients, one row each (age, severity, new, stay); no grouping factor.
ROS ChileSchools example (chile_schools.R): regression-discontinuity stan_glm(read92 ~ eligible + rule2); one row per school, cmb_regn a 4-level combined region (covariate), no repeated cluster.
ROS Congress example: wide table, one row per congressional district with 3 election years (inc86/88/90, v86/88/90); wide repeated-measures layout, no grouping column.
ROS Coins/HeadsSchools example: 11-row frequency table (x = number of heads, count); a histogram, no grouping factor.
ROS ElectionsEconomy (Hibbs bread-and-peace): 16 elections, vote ~ growth; one point per election year, a time series with no replication.
ROS Incentives example: 62 rows (rr_diff, value, prepay, gift, burden); meta-analysis of survey-incentive conditions with no study/survey id column in the table, no grouping factor.
ROS KidIQ example: classical lm(kid_score ~ mom_hs + mom_iq + ...); one row per child, no grouping factor (same data as stan_arm kidiq).
ROS LowBwt example: Hosmer-Lemeshow low-birth-weight data, one row per infant (ID row id); glm(low ~ ...), no grouping factor.
ROS Mesquite example: lm(weight ~ diam + height + density + group); group a 2-level site/batch covariate, 46 bushes one row each, no clustering unit (as stan_arm mesquite).
ROS Mile example: world-record mile times by year, 32-row time series, no replication.
ROS Gay example: 81422 respondents x 7 columns (age, gender, race, gay-marriage attitudes); no state or cluster column in this extract, one row per respondent.

ROS AcademyAwards data (oscars.csv/txt): no model script in the repo and no documented response. Comp (318 competition/choice sets) repeats and would support a conditional-logit Oscar-winner model, but no column is a clean per-competition winner (PrW takes 0/1/2/3 and sums to 0 for most Comps), so there is no defensible response. RULE GAP: a repeating choice-set grouping with no identifiable response; excluded rather than guess a winner column.
ROS Poststrat poll (rda twin of Poststrat/data/poll.csv): 778 respondents, vote and pid only, no sampling cluster.
ROS Pollution (rda twin of pollution.csv): 60 cities one row each, no grouping factor.
ROS RiskyBehavior (rda twin of risky.csv): one row per subject, Poisson count outcome, no grouping factor.
ROS Coop example: 27 rows, candidate names with vote tallies at 6 time points (V2-V7); a wide election-count time series, no grouping column.
ROS Roaches (rda twin of roaches.csv): one row per apartment, Poisson count, no grouping factor.
ROS SexRatio example: 5-row aggregate (x attractiveness, y percent girls); no grouping, no replication.
ROS Student (rda twin of student-merged.csv): one row per student; school is a 2-level fixed predictor used among 26 covariates (stan_glm(G3mat ~ .)), not a sampling cluster.
ROS Arsenic/Wells example: glm(switched ~ dist + arsenic + educ, binomial); one row per household, no grouping factor (as stan_arm wells).
7-column model extract of the NYC HVS rodent data (y, race, floor, dist, bldg); same 15894 apartments as Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed), derived.
1748-row subset of apt.dat / the HVS rodent data, derived.
54-column all-variables version of the HVS rodent apartment data (15894 rows); duplicate of Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed).
459-row subset of the HVS rodent data, derived.
20-column unsorted version of Rodents/hvs02_sorted.csv (filed), same 15894 rows, duplicate.
